speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you've had any recent head injuries, seizures, or a history of meningitis? Also, are you experiencing a stiff neck or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your altered mentation and history of haloperidol use, I need to rule out Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome; do you have any muscle rigidity or difficulty swallowing? Also, has anyone noticed any changes in your skin color or sweating patterns?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall starting or increasing your haloperidol dose recently, and have you noticed any darkening of your urine? REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase, Complete Blood Count, and Electrolytes.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated); Complete Blood Count: White Blood Cell Count 14,700/mm3 (elevated); Electrolytes: Data not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated creatine kinase and muscle rigidity strongly suggest Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, but I need to confirm your renal function and temperature. What is your current blood pressure and heart rate, and have your recent electrolyte results shown any abnormalities?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of tics, currently on a low dose of haloperidol. Social history: Patient details on social and occupational history not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Electrolytes, Blood Urea Nitrogen, Creatinine, and Liver Function Tests. Do you have a current temperature reading, and has your urine output decreased or changed in color?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrolytes: Data not provided; Blood Urea Nitrogen: Data not provided; Creatinine: Data not provided; Liver Function Tests: Data not provided; Temperature: 39.6°C (103.2°F); Urine Output/Color: Data not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: The high fever of 39.6°C, severe rigidity, confusion, and markedly elevated creatine kinase in a patient on haloperidol are classic signs of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
